# PLAN — iteration 3
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent uses 7 LUTs and 9 FFs and meets timing, so this iteration must strictly reduce LUTs to improve the objective. Iteration 1’s 8-bit natural-wrap counter increased LUTs to 10; iteration 2’s comparator rewrite left LUTs and FFs unchanged. The seed retains a 32-bit counter with explicit terminal-count wrap logic, while the top’s numeric latency is unknown; preserve its observable cycles and do not add an annotation.

## Hypothesis
Replacing the counter’s increment-and-wrap mux with explicit per-bit toggle equations may let Vivado share the modulo-256 carry and wrap logic, reducing LUTs while keeping the 9 FFs and registered PWM output.

## Instruction for generator
Keep the existing `counter < {24'd0, duty}` comparison and registered `pwm_out` assignment unchanged. Replace only the counter update with an 8-bit modulo-256 counter expressed as per-bit toggles: bit 0 toggles each active cycle, and each higher bit toggles when all lower bits are one; preserve synchronous reset to zero. This differs from iteration 1’s narrowed counter using a whole-vector `+ 1` expression; preserve the exact post-reset 0–255 sequence and assess the result against the 7-LUT incumbent under the fixed verification and routed timing gates.
